what_it_does: This paper addresses the design of millimeter-wave receivers—the radio-frequency front-end circuits in 5G and radar systems. These receivers must simultaneously achieve three difficult goals: catch very weak signals with minimal electrical noise, handle strong interfering signals without distortion, and sharply filter out unwanted frequencies. Existing designs sacrifice one goal to achieve the others. This work introduces a novel passive feedforward path that cancels interfering signals before they hit the nonlinear components (where distortion happens), enabling sharp filtering while keeping noise low and linearity high.
